title: Affect as Attack
one_line: Can an emotion pushed directly into a language model's hidden state switch off its safety guardrail, even though the prompt looks harmless?

model.why: The proposal's model: strong refusal (84% of HarmBench requests refused), Llama Scope SAEs, the reference model of the refusal-direction literature, runs at about 270 tok/s batched on the M5 Pro. Final choice confirmed by E00 and the model study.

findings.text: Removing one direction (layer 11) takes Llama 3.1 8B from 14.5% to 84.9% harmful answers on HarmBench, with no new refusals on harmless requests.
The proposal's paired emotion vectors share one large common direction (emotional versus flat writing); the emotion-specific part is tested separately.

Close prior work exists: Sun et al. 2026 steer a valence-arousal plane in Llama 3.1 8B against HarmBench, and RepE (2023) broke refusal with a happiness vector. The project's gap is narrower than the proposal says.
About ten references in the proposal could not be found as cited (placeholder arXiv ids); the audit lists real replacements.

blockers.text: Hugging Face token has no accepted Llama licence (403). Using the ungated unsloth mirror of the same weights; accept the Meta licence on huggingface.co to be clean.
